title: He Escaped an 'Escape-Proof' Jail With a Wooden Gun
style: flat cartoon silhouettes, 1930s noir palette, cuts locked to the music's beat; a few real PD photos as evidence inserts
lines: In 1934, America's most wanted man broke out of an escape proof jail. His weapon? A gun carved out of wood. And blackened with shoe polish.
His name was John Dillinger. An Indiana farm boy who robbed a grocer at twenty one, and got ten years in prison.
Prison didn't fix him. It trained him. Inside, he met the bank robbers who would become his gang.
Paroled in 1933, he went on a bank robbing spree across the Midwest. Fast. Polite. Almost theatrical. He would vault right over the counter.
Then he did something nobody saw coming. He smuggled guns into his old prison, and ten of his friends broke out.
Weeks later, they returned the favor, and broke him out of a jail in Ohio. A sheriff was killed that night.
January 1934. A hotel fire in Tucson, Arizona. Firemen recognized the gang from a detective magazine. Dillinger was arrested without a shot.
They sent him to Crown Point, Indiana. A jail the newspapers called escape proof.
There, he posed for a famous photo, his arm around the prosecutor's shoulder. Smiling.
Five weeks later, on March 3rd, he made his move.
He pulled out a pistol carved from wood, blackened with shoe polish. And the guards believed it.
He locked the guards in a cell, grabbed two real machine guns, and walked out the front.
Then he stole the sheriff's own car, and drove it across the state line. That was his biggest mistake.
A stolen car across a state line was a federal crime. Now J. Edgar Hoover's agents were coming for him.
He became Public Enemy Number One. He burned off his fingerprints with acid, and had surgery to change his face.
July 22nd, 1934. Chicago. A woman in an orange dress walked out of a movie theater beside him. She had sold him out.
Federal agents were waiting. Dillinger ran for an alley. He was shot dead. He was thirty one.
But here's the twist. Did he really carve that gun himself? Many believe it was smuggled in, with a bribe.
And some still think the man in that alley wasn't Dillinger at all. In 2019, his family tried to dig him up to find out. A court said no.
What do you think? Was it him? Tell me in the comments. Then watch our Alcatraz short, three men who escaped and were never found. And follow for a new mystery every day.

notes: Sources: FBI History 'John Dillinger' (fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/john-dillinger); Wikipedia 'John Dillinger'; Indiana Historical Bureau; AP 2019-2020 coverage of the exhumation request (Crown Hill Cemetery; Marion County judge blocked it). Born 1903 Indianapolis, family moved to a farm near Mooresville. 1924 robbed a Mooresville grocer, sentenced 10-20 years; met Harry Pierpont and others in prison. Paroled May 1933; bank robberies; known for vaulting counters. Sept 1933: guns smuggled into Indiana State Prison, 10 inmates escaped. Oct 1933: gang broke him out of Allen County jail, Lima, Ohio; Sheriff Jess Sarber killed. 22-25 Jan 1934: Hotel Congress fire, Tucson; firemen recognized gang members from True Detective; arrested. Sent to Lake County jail, Crown Point, called escape-proof; famous photo with prosecutor Robert Estill. 3 Mar 1934: wooden gun escape, took two machine guns, stole Sheriff Lillian Holley's car, crossed into Illinois -> federal Dyer Act, Bureau of Investigation pursuit. Public Enemy No. 1; acid on fingertips and facial surgery (May 1934). 22 Jul 1934: Biograph Theater, Chicago; Ana Cumpănaș (Anna Sage, 'woman in red', dress was orange) tipped the Bureau; shot in alley; age 31. Wooden gun: Dillinger claimed he whittled it; many investigators/historians believe it was smuggled in via bribery. 2019 family exhumation plan; court blocked it (Dec 2020 ruling).
